alkeyword.com — Research

Date: 2026-08-10 Concept: al- (alchemy/algebra/algorithm) + keyword. Bring only a domain name. The program visits the site, reads it, and generates more content for it. Status: Research + direction. No build decision made.

0. Domain state

Registered via Amazon Registrar, Cloudflare NS, created 2025-04-01, expires 2027-04-01. Currently serves a live page titled "Alkeyword — Observable Type Safety for Elixir." Repurposing displaces that.

2. ⚠️ "Bring only your domain" is already table stakes

This is the finding that should shape the build. The domain-only onboarding is not a wedge — there is an entire established segment doing exactly it:

ToolPitch
Keywordly Auto-Pilot"Enter your domain so we analyze your niche and audience"
BlogSEO"analyzes your site, writes daily articles matching your brand voice, publishes automatically"
WPAutoBlog"We automatically analyze your website to create your content plan based on your niche"
Frizerly"30+ articles per month, no manual effort"
Satellitor / BlogBuster / SEOWriting / auto-post.io / Sight AI / AutoSEOsame shape

They also mostly solve publishing (WordPress/Ghost/Shopify OAuth), which is the expensive part.

But this segment is selling directly into a penalty. Google's March 2026 core update named scaled content abuse as a primary target: sites publishing hundreds/thousands of AI pages without editorial oversight saw 50–80% traffic drops, and manual actions are now being issued. "30+ articles/month, no manual effort" is a description of the penalized behavior.

So: the input is commoditized, the volume play is radioactive, and the whole segment is optimizing for a Google surface whose overlap with AI citations has collapsed below 20%.

That's not a dead end — it's a very specific opening.

3. The wedge: transmutation, not fabrication

The name is the strategy. Alchemy transmutes existing material; it doesn't conjure from nothing.

Every autoblog tool fabricates: it guesses your niche and writes net-new articles about it. That's why they hallucinate about the business, why the output is generic, and why it trips scaled-content-abuse detection.

The alchemy version: the site's own crawled content is the raw material. Extract every fact, number, claim, product, price, process, person, and location the site already states — then recombine those into the page forms AI engines actually cite. Every generated sentence traces back to the source page it came from.

This is defensible on four axes at once:

  1. Grounded. Nothing is invented, so it can't be wrong about the business. (RAG grounding: up

to −71% hallucination.)

  1. Penalty-resistant. It's genuinely, specifically about that business — the opposite of spun

keyword pages. Cap output deliberately (see §5).

  1. Differentiated. None of the ten tools above do this; they all start from a niche guess.

  2. On-target for GEO. The forms it produces are exactly the measured +40% levers — statistics,

quotations, citations, authoritative language.

Forms worth minting from a crawl

  • Comparison pages (X vs Y) — highest citation pull in AI answers

  • Definition / glossary pages — Wikipedia-shaped, disproportionately cited

  • FAQ pages answering the literal questions people type into engines

  • Data / statistics pages — the single strongest measured citation lever

  • "How it works" explainers built from processes described across scattered pages

  • Entity / about pages that correct what models currently get wrong about the brand

4. The sharp version: crawl → probe → close the delta

This is the part that makes it a product rather than a generator.

1. CRAWL      the domain. Build a graph of what the site actually claims.
2. PROBE      the engines. Ask ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini/AIO about this brand
              and its category. Record what they say and what they cite.
3. DIFF       the two.
                • facts the site states that the models don't know
                • things the models say about the brand that are WRONG
                • questions the models answer with a competitor cited
                • claims the site makes with no supporting page to cite
4. GENERATE   content that closes exactly those gaps, grounded in step 1.
5. RE-PROBE   in 30 days. Did the gap close?

Why this matters: it gives generation a measurable target. No autoblog tool has one — they publish on a schedule and hope. This produces a before/after proof loop, which is the exact thing whose absence is causing churn across the whole GEO category ("brands watch flat dashboards for 6 months and churn").

It also inverts the standard product: the tracker crowd measures and never acts; the autoblog crowd acts and never measures. This does both, and the measurement aims the action.

5. Deliberate constraints (these are features)

  • Cap output. Sell "6 pieces that close 6 measured gaps," never "30 articles a month." The

volume pitch is the penalty pitch. This is also a cost control.

  • Human approval by default. Generate → review → publish. Fully-automatic publishing is where

brand risk and Google risk both live.

  • Provenance on every claim. Each generated assertion links to the source page it came from.

This is the trust story and the demo — hover a sentence, see where it came from.

  • Refuse when the raw material is too thin. A 3-page brochure site has nothing to transmute.

Say so rather than fabricating. This is what distinguishes the product from the segment.

6. Open problems

Where does the content go? Domain-only input means no credentials, so v1 is generate + export (markdown / HTML / PDF) with CMS detected from the crawl and the right handoff offered. Publishing integrations (WordPress ≈ 40% of the web, Webflow, Shopify, Ghost) are the obvious v2 and the thing the incumbents already have. Not a blocker, but don't underestimate it.

Unbounded crawl+generate cost per signup. Anyone can paste any domain. Gate it: crawl + gap report is cheap and becomes the free tier; generation is expensive and is the paid action. That split also happens to be the right funnel.

Demand signal without keyword data. You have no volume numbers from a domain alone — but for GEO the unit of demand is a question, not a keyword with a volume figure, and the question set comes from the probe step. The missing keyword data is only a problem if you're building an SEO tool. Build the GEO tool.

7. Stack fit

This maps onto tooling that already exists in this portfolio more than incidentally: crawl → build a claim graph → extract edges → find structural gaps → trace every generated statement back along an evidence path. That is Graphonomous's shape (knowledge graph, edge extraction, evidence-path tracing, belief revision when a crawl contradicts a prior crawl). Worth evaluating as the engine rather than building claim-graph infrastructure from scratch.

8. On the name

al- as in alchemy/algebra/algorithm is a coherent, defensible logic, and "transmute what you already have into gold" is a genuinely good brand story that the product actually delivers on.

Remaining real issue: it fails the radio test — said aloud, most people won't spell it right, and some will hear "AI keyword." Mitigate by making the alchemy framing loud and immediate on the page (the wordmark, the metaphor, the copy) so the al- reads as intentional within two seconds.

Secondary tension: "keyword" anchors to 2015 SEO, while §3–4 argue the unit is a question, not a keyword. Livable — "keyword" is category-legible and gets you found — but the copy should resolve it rather than ignore it.
